title: Distinguished-ideal rig-regular formal pairs and formal blowups
statement: Use the formal spectra and completions of [def-per-adic-formal-completion], the absolute nonregular ideal of [def-per-formal-completion-geometry], and the formal-affine Noetherian, reduced, quasi-excellent and regular-map predicates of [def-per-adic-formal-geometry]. A formal ideal on a ringed space is its family of ideals in the stalks. It is coherent, in the local finite-generation sense of [pqf-def-coherent], when locally those stalk ideals are generated by germs of finitely many sections, invertible when locally generated by one section whose germ is a non-zero-divisor at every point, and open relative to a distinguished ideal when it contains a positive power of that ideal. Extension means ideal extension along the actual stalk maps. For a scheme ideal its stalk ideal is generated by germs of its sections on affine opens; completion extends this family along the canonical completion map. A complete formal affine chart is an open immersion from Spf(B,K), B Noetherian and K-adically complete, identifying the extended K with the distinguished ideal. A distinguished-ideal Noetherian formal pair consists of a Noetherian formal ringed space and a coherent ideal locally identified by such charts. Its regularity means regularity of all complete chart rings [def-weil-regular-scheme]; its singular locus is the chartwise nonregular locus of Spec(B), restricted to formal points. A formal variety component has a reduced closed-fibre scheme: a homeomorphism from a reduced scheme with surjective stalk maps and kernel the radical of the distinguished stalk ideal, with a finite-type structure map to a characteristic-zero field [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A finite union of such components means a finite disjoint open cover, permitting different fields and the empty cover. A rig-regular input is such a pair over Q, reduced and quasi-excellent, with invertible distinguished ideal, a finite union of formal varieties, and on each complete chart a positive power of K contained in the absolute singular ideal. A regular map of pairs preserves the distinguished ideals, is local on stalks, and is regular on all formal affine opens using the recorded section-map predicate. For a coherent open ideal J a formal blowup is, on an open formal affine cover, the completion of the ordinary blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] of Spec(B) in a finite-type ideal whose completion is J; the square over that target chart is cartesian and its composite to Spec(B) is the ordinary blowup map after completion. Its distinguished ideal is extended from the base. The center is regular if locally it is defined by an ideal containing a positive power of K whose ordinary quotient scheme is regular. These are constructions and predicates, not existence assertions.
